name: Chengdu Rongcheng (成都蓉城)
verdict: The club's own 成都蓉城 wordmark forms part of Chengdu Rongcheng's chest advertisement in CSL play, alongside group sibling Chengdu Jian Gong; the club company is 95% owned by Chengdu Xingcheng Investment Group.

why.text: The 成都蓉城 wordmark on the shirt is the brand of Chengdu Rongcheng FC, a company 95% owned by Chengdu Xingcheng Investment Group, whose controlling shareholder with 90% is the Chengdu municipal state-assets commission. The UN human rights office found in 2022 that serious human rights violations had been committed against Uyghurs and other mostly Muslim communities in Xinjiang, including large-scale arbitrary detention that may amount to crimes against humanity. So the money behind the shirt's 成都蓉城 branding is the Chinese state's.
why.messageLine: The UN human rights office found that China's large-scale arbitrary detention of Uyghurs in Xinjiang may amount to crimes against humanity.

note: Not the football club's record here (this is a sponsor record for the club wordmark printed as part of the chest advertisement). Rating note: proposed 'serious' — the Chinese state controls the sponsor (the link, claims chengdu-rongcheng-club-xingcheng-ownership + xingcheng-group-sasac-ownership: the club company is 95% owned by Chengdu Xingcheng Investment Group, whose controlling shareholder with 90% is Chengdu SASAC; METHOD.md counts control), and the record (claim china-xinjiang-un-assessment) is documented for that state. The club wordmark and Chengdu Jian Gong share the same parent group, so the chest ad advertises within one state-owned group ('羊毛出在羊身上', as Tencent News put it).
